extracted.intended_audience: permanent secretaries, directors general, chief executives of arm’s length bodies, senior leaders and board members, those commissioning communication, communication leads and practitioners, and third parties engaged in government communication
extracted.subtask_description: A government functional standard setting mandatory and advisory expectations for planning, delivering and managing government communication (campaigns, packages, media, digital, insight, marketing, internal and external affairs) to support HM Government policy and public services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives aligned to government policy and organisational objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall have objectives aligned to government policy and organisational objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure campaign and communication objectives support the policy aim and demonstrate how communication contributes to achieving the policy aim (see 5.2). Objectives should be outcome-focused and align with government-wide plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote a shared vision across government
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall promote a shared vision across government, ensuring they meet the needs of government as a whole in relation to policy and strategic objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work collaboratively across departments to ensure consistency with cross-government priorities and reduce duplication and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Champion a unified response to crisis and emergency management
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall champion a unified response to crisis and emergency management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate communications across stakeholders and follow crisis communication plans to ensure timely, accurate and consistent messaging (see 7.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote diversity and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall promote a culture of diversity and inclusion which represents the society served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor equality, diversity and inclusion principles into recruitment, team-building and communications planning (see 7.2.2 and referenced GCS EDI guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear tiered accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall ensure, through tiered accountability, that it is clear who makes decisions and owns outcomes and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define roles and accountabilities in the governance and management framework; assign responsibilities to people with appropriate seniority, skills and experience (see 4.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative working for clear, simple and consistent communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall work collaboratively in order to achieve clear, simple and consistent communication on behalf of government; managing duplication and minimising complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate communications with other functions and across government to maintain coherence and reduce contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple, proportionate and user-focused processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall keep processes simple, proportionate and user-focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design governance and delivery processes that are not unnecessarily complex and focus on user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous improvement, efficiency, innovation and value for money
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall promote opportunities for continuous improvement, efficiency, innovation and transformation where this represents value for money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture lessons, evaluate effectiveness, and apply improvements; plan resources and capability to deliver contemporary technologies and methods (see 7.10, 7.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold public service codes of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication shall uphold public service codes of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure communicators adhere to the Civil Service Code and related propriety and ethics guidance (see 7.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined governance and management framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A governance and management framework shall be defined and established across government, and within organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should set authority limits, decision‑making roles, reporting, accountabilities, assurance needs and associated documentation (see Glossary 'governance and management framework').

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-government policy, directives and guidance availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-government policy, directives and guidance relating to the management of government communication should be defined, kept up to date and be communicated to and available for the use of organisational communication teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Modern Communications Operating Model and central professional guidance to inform local practice (see 4.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign governance using OASIS lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Each campaign shall be undertaken in accordance with the Objectives, Audience Insight, Strategy, Implementation, Scoring (OASIS) campaign life cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a named campaign commissioner and head of campaign who will agree objectives and define roles, responsibilities, strategy, plan and resources (see 4.1.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spend controls and compliance for advertising/marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: HM Government organisations shall comply with GovS 006, Finance, and communications advertising, marketing and communications spend controls on campaigns or programmes with a value of £100,000 or over (per year) in accordance with GovS 008, Commercial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek written approvals where required; obtain ministerial and senior officer approvals before submitting expenditure approval applications; follow Cabinet Office spend controls and seek cross‑function advice in advance (see 4.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual organisational communication plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Each organisation shall prepare a communication plan annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan shall demonstrate how the organisation’s communication supports the government-wide communication plan, outline how communication supports delivery of policies and services, include outcome-based metrics, be agreed by the senior officer accountable and approved at executive board level (see 4.2.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate assurance framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisations should have a defined and established approach to assurance, which should be applied proportionately to the risk and value of the activity, and integrated with the organisation’s overall assurance framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance should typically operate on at least three levels (operational management, senior independent management, independent bodies); plan assurance activity to minimise disruption and avoid duplication; focus assurance on requirements and audiences (see 4.3.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely, criteria-based decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions relating to communication management should be made and approvals given in a timely manner, in accordance with the organisation’s communication governance and management framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess options against defined criteria, consult stakeholders and subject matter experts, and take holistic account of context, risks and stakeholder reactions; seek other functions' advice where necessary (see 4.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined roles and accountabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles and accountabilities shall be defined in the organisation’s governance and management framework and assigned to people with appropriate seniority, skills and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should include activities, outputs or outcomes they are responsible for and the person they are accountable to (see 4.5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior officer accountable for communication across government (role responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The senior officer accountable for communication across government is accountable to ministers for the efficient and effective operation of government-wide communication and is responsible for the government’s communication strategy, effectiveness and efficiency of government communication, advice to ministers, major cross-government campaigns, the government’s communication plan and standards of professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This role (CEO for Government communication/GCS lead) provides cross-government leadership and approves major spending and procurement decisions (see 4.5.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior officer accountable for a communications discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: A senior officer accountable for a specific communications discipline is accountable for leading continuous improvement and professional development of their communication discipline, building capability, overseeing cross-government networks and commissioning guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This role is a corporate contribution and should allocate time (e.g., 20%) to support the wider profession (see 4.5.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting officer stewardship for communication resources
rubrics_metrics.description: An organisation’s Accounting Officer is accountable to Parliament and the public for the stewardship of public resources, including for communication, ensuring they are used effectively and to high standards of probity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure communications expenditure and resource use follow financial governance and public accountability expectations (see 4.5.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior officer accountable for an organisation’s communication (role responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The senior officer accountable for an organisation’s communication is accountable for developing the scope of communication, setting objectives, developing governance and management frameworks, maintaining the organisation’s communication plan and grid, setting performance measures, ensuring resources and building capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In departments this role is usually Director or Head of Communication; they must ensure plans and measures are in place and resourced appropriately (see 4.5.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication commissioner responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication commissioner is accountable for setting a campaign’s objectives and ensuring they are fulfilled, keeping senior leadership informed, defining desired outcomes with the head of campaign, advising on escalated issues and approving changes to the campaign plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This role (campaign lead/head of discipline) owns objectives and oversight and coordinates with the head of campaign (see 4.5.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Head of campaign responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A head of a campaign is accountable for developing and managing a campaign day-to-day: mobilising, briefing and motivating the team; developing and managing the campaign plan; managing issues and risks; and evaluating outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep campaign commissioner informed, escalate risks appropriately, and take corrective action as needed (see 4.5.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication lead for a package responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication lead for a communication package is accountable for managing assigned work: ensuring work completed within constraints, planning, monitoring, forecasting, reporting progress, managing risks and requesting scope changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate within the campaign plan and escalate issues that cannot be resolved locally (see 4.5.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication business partnering
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication business partners work directly with teams to build local, specialist knowledge and ensure communication advice is integrated in planning and decision-making from the outset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business partners should be expert communicators aligned with Government Communication Service business partnering guidance (see 4.5.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Government Communication Service codes of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff engaged in communication activity shall follow and be subject to the Government Communication Service’s codes of practice in their communication activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to professional standards and codes as defined by GCS (see 4.5.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign planning using OASIS lifecycle and audience perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Each campaign shall be undertaken in accordance with the OASIS campaign life cycle which enables problems to be addressed from an audience perspective, a united course of action and coordinated implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan campaigns with head of campaign and commissioner, draw lessons from previous campaigns, and follow the OASIS model for Objectives, Audience Insight, Strategy, Implementation, Scoring (see 5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign objectives: measurable, achievable and outcome-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaign objectives should be achievable, measurable (expressed numerically), focused on outcomes not outputs, and related to changing attitudes and/or behaviour. When objectives cannot be measured numerically, the criteria for validating their achievement should be defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link objectives to policy aims and ensure they can be evaluated using the Government Communication Service Evaluation Framework (see 5.2, note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience insight driven by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns should use data to generate insights determining the target audience’s attitudes, habits and preferences so that government communication can be relevant, meaningful and effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on quantitative and qualitative sources, commissioned and publicly available, and conduct analysis in accordance with GovS 010 (see 5.3 and 6.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign strategy components
rubrics_metrics.description: The campaign strategy shall include: a defined target audience, a proposition, messages, and a channel strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience insight to set the strategic approach and ensure integration across channels and disciplines (see 5.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive campaign plan elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The campaign plan should include: the objective; purpose of the campaign; audience; internal and external issues; messages; channels; accountabilities; measurement; approach; timescales; resources required; influencers to engage; partners to be involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the plan channel-agnostically, pilot approaches against evaluation criteria, monitor outputs/outtakes/outcomes and take corrective action where necessary (see 5.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel-agnostic planning and piloting
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaign planning should be developed using a channel-agnostic approach, choosing the most appropriate channel or combination to achieve objectives and piloting to verify effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot and measure chosen approaches; adjust plan if pilots indicate different approaches needed (see 5.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor outputs, outtakes and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The campaign should be rolled out with progress monitored in terms of outputs, outtakes and outcomes and evaluated once complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate approximately 5%–10% of total campaign expenditure to evaluation; analysis shall be undertaken in accordance with GovS 010 (see 5.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic communication: alignment and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic communication should be aligned to the delivery of HM Government priorities, planned using defined practices, focused on audience understanding, evaluated to demonstrate value and integrated with all other aspects of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic communicators should work alongside policy, operations, HR and project delivery colleagues from the outset; use forward-planning grids and research to inform planning (see 6.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital communication: skills, structure and continuous learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicators should master new techniques, maintain up-to-date digital skills and structure teams around core digital functions: strategy & leadership, data & insight analysis, technical content creation, and copywriting/editing/channel management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure teams include generalist digital experts and specialists; manage work and data in accordance with GovS 005 (see 6.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & Insight: use diverse data sources and robust analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Government communicators should draw on a range of data sources – quantitative and qualitative, commissioned and publicly available – to create a full picture of target audiences and identify appropriate reach methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data to personalise and target messages; conduct analysis in line with GovS 010 (see 6.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing: evidence-based, measurable and service-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing channels should support awareness, influence attitudes and behaviours; be founded on behavioural science and research, based on reliable data, use validated creative approaches, be measurable, focus on high-quality end-to-end service and customer experience, aid operations and build trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply analysis per GovS 010 and follow guidance on buying advertising and marketing services (see 6.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership marketing: in‑kind, assessed and governed
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnership marketing shall be negotiated on an in‑kind basis; partners shall not be required to pay a fee to be associated with a campaign; objectives defined and potential partners assessed against reach, relevance and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw a partnership agreement covering requirements, roles, embargoes, resources, budget, data security, governance, risk and performance indicators; manage relationships per agreement and escalate to project delivery/commercial standards when significant (see 6.5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations: honesty, planning and cross-platform expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Media relations operations shall explain policies and services through media partners, maintain a media planning schedule and forward look, and practitioners should be prepared to communicate with honesty and evidence across broadcast, print and online platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include proactive/reactive handling, crisis management, relationship management with journalists and ministers, content creation, and impact tracking (see 6.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: External affairs: intelligence, balance and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: External affairs practitioners should gather intelligence to inform internal thinking, take a balanced approach encouraging supportive voices and mitigating criticism, explain policies to influential individuals and coordinate high-level stakeholder engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intelligence to provide early warning of issues and evaluate impacts of campaigns (see 6.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal communication: strategy and employee engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisations should develop an internal communication strategy to inform and engage employees, helping them see the connection between their job and organisational vision and improving manager-team communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal communication should add value, support reputation and brand, be agreed with commissioning managers, be authentic, achievable, actionable and compelling, engage line managers and consider employees’ views (see 6.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability and capacity planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Management shall balance supply and demand for communication resources and maintain a comprehensive view of future resource needs, identifying and addressing shortfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure planned resources include expertise in contemporary technologies and online platforms; prioritise work to meet planned needs (see 7.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Building capability and talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior officers shall champion GCS talent schemes and training, use careers guidance to clarify skills by grade, and ensure managers conduct career conversations and include relevant professional development in Personal Development Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Government Communication Service Career Framework and training offers to build workforce capability (see 7.2.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Build diverse and effective teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams shall draw talent from every section of society; senior officers and campaign leads should ensure GCS principles and best practice are considered in recruitment and planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote careers across the UK and follow GCS equality, diversity and location strategies (see 7.2.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety and ethics: objectivity and non-partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Government communicators shall carry out their work objectively and without political bias, in accordance with the Civil Service Code and propriety guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior officers must ensure communicators know responsibilities and how to raise concerns; propriety means presenting government policies properly and effectively (see 7.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data handling and protection compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior officers and campaign leads shall review data guidance regularly and ensure compliance within their teams, taking account of emerging technologies such as AI and digital channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage data in accordance with GovS 005 and Government Communication Service data guidance (see 7.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior officers and those responsible for campaigns shall follow GCS guidance to create accessible and inclusive content and channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure publications and channels meet accessibility best practice and legal requirements (see 7.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Government departments, agencies and arm’s length bodies shall comply with the HM Government identity guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect Royal Coat of Arms usage restrictions and apply official brand guidance and artwork (see 7.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication planning and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A crisis communication plan should be developed and validated in advance for known risks and should aim to keep stakeholders informed, build public trust, ensure accurate media reporting and recover reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan should include affected groups, worst-case scenarios, key messages, channels and roles; update as situation evolves, communicate openly and transparently based on established facts, and advise senior management (see 7.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviour change considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviour change should be considered in campaigns; identify behaviours necessary to meet policy objectives and barriers to change, and include addressable behaviours in planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether audiences have the skills, resources/support and motivation to change; use behaviour change guidance and project delivery links where relevant (see 7.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style: clear, concise and consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication should be written using the most appropriate language to engage target audiences and achieve objectives; writing should be clear, concise and consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the GCS Style Guide for tone, plain English and accessibility (see 7.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning from experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessons should be continually captured, evaluated and action taken to mitigate risk and facilitate continual improvement, including an evidence base of what techniques work with different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use post-campaign evaluation and learning to improve future practice and to avoid repeating mistakes (see 7.10).
